mainTopic: The nine כהנים who carry the תמיד, how the lamb was tied, the tables of the מקדש, and where the תמיד was slaughtered.
overview: The משנה lists nine כהנים in order. Six carry the parts of the תמיד lamb, and the משנה explains exactly how each part is held. Three more carry the סולת, the חביתין, and the wine. Everything is placed on the lower western half of the כבש and salted, and the כהנים go to לשכת הגזית to say קריאת שמע. The גמרא explains that the lamb was tied foreleg to hind leg, like עקידת יצחק. It then gives two reasons why all four legs were not tied together (כפיתה): disgrace to holy things, or copying the ways of the nations. It quotes a משנה listing the thirteen tables in the מקדש and explains that marble was used because metal heats up. Next, it learns from 'שנים ליום' that the תמיד is slaughtered facing the daylight. The amud ends by opening the story of the ten questions אלכסנדרוס מוקדון asked the זקני הנגב, and the questions themselves come on the next amud.

steps.title: The first priest carries the head and the right hind leg
steps.stepSummary: The first כהן carries the head in his right hand and the right hind leg in his left hand. The משנה spells out how each piece is positioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first priest carries the head and a leg. The head is in his right hand, with its nose toward his arm, its horns between his fingers, and the cut side of the neck facing up, covered by fat. The right hind leg is in his left hand, with the skin side facing out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins its list of the nine כהנים who carry the parts of the תמיד. It starts with the first כהן, who carries the head and the right hind leg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head is the most important part, so it goes in the right hand. The fat (פדר) is placed over the neck to cover the bloody place of שחיטה. The leg is held with the skin side out, not the cut side.

keyTerms.meaning: The place on the neck where the animal was slaughtered
Fat, used here to cover the place of slaughter
The skin side of the limb, its outer side
Nose or snout

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה, רגל means a HIND leg. The forelegs are called ידים, which you will see in the next step.

phrases.english: The first – with the head and with the leg.
phrases.notes: This is the right hind leg, as the משנה says a few lines later.

phrases.english: The head in his right hand,
and its nose toward his arm,
its horns between his fingers,
the place of its slaughter on top,
and the fat placed upon it.
The right leg in his left hand,
and the skin side facing out.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first כהן carries the head in his right hand, positioned with the neck up and covered with fat, and the right hind leg in his left hand, skin side out.

steps.title: The second priest carries the two forelegs
steps.stepSummary: The second כהן carries both forelegs, right in his right hand and left in his left, with the skin side facing out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second priest carries the two forelegs. The right one is in his right hand and the left one is in his left hand, with the skin side facing out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the list with the second כהן, who carries the two forelegs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step is simple: each foreleg goes in the matching hand. The rule from step 1 repeats here, that the skin side faces outward.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the forelegs of the animal

phrases.english: The second – with the two forelegs,
the right one in his right hand,
and the left one in his left hand,
and the skin side facing out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second כהן carries both forelegs, each in the matching hand, skin side out.

steps.title: The third priest carries the haunch and the left hind leg
steps.stepSummary: The third כהן carries the haunch with the tail, the lobe of the liver, and the kidneys in his right hand, and the left hind leg in his left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The third priest carries the haunch and a leg. The haunch is in his right hand, with the tail hanging between his fingers, and the finger-like lobe of the liver and the two kidneys go with it. The left hind leg is in his left hand, with the skin side facing out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the third כהן, who carries the back end of the animal and the left hind leg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עוקץ (haunch) comes with the אליה (tail) still attached and hanging down. The אצבע הכבד and the two kidneys are also carried with it. The other hind leg, the left one, is carried by this כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The haunch, the rear end of the animal
The fat tail of the sheep
Hanging down loosely
The finger-like lobe of the liver
Kidneys

phrases.english: The third – with the haunch and with the leg.
The haunch in his right hand,
and the tail hanging down between his fingers,
and the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys with it.
The left leg in his left hand,
and the skin side facing out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third כהן carries the haunch with the tail, the liver lobe, and the kidneys in his right hand, and the left hind leg in his left hand.

steps.title: The fourth priest carries the breast and the neck section
steps.stepSummary: The fourth כהן carries the חזה in his right hand and the גרה in his left hand, with ribs held between his fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The fourth priest carries the breast and the neck section. The breast is in his right hand and the neck section is in his left, and its ribs are between his two fingers.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the fourth כהן, who carries the chest area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The more important piece, the חזה, again goes in the right hand. Ribs stay attached and are held between his fingers.

keyTerms.meaning: The breast of the animal
The neck section, where the cud passes
Ribs

phrases.english: The fourth – with the breast and with the neck section.
The breast in his right hand and the neck section in his left,
and its ribs between his two fingers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth כהן carries the חזה in his right hand and the גרה, with ribs attached, in his left hand.

steps.title: The fifth priest carries the two flanks
steps.stepSummary: The fifth כהן carries the two sides of the animal, each in the matching hand, skin side out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The fifth priest carries the two flanks. The right one is in his right hand and the left one is in his left hand, with the skin side facing out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the fifth כהן, who carries the two side sections of the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the second כהן in step 2: two matching pieces, one in each hand, skin side out.

keyTerms.meaning: The flanks, the side sections of the animal

phrases.english: The fifth – with the two flanks,
the right one in his right hand,
and the left one in his left hand,
and the skin side facing out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of כהנים, using the same pattern as step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fifth כהן carries the two flanks, each in the matching hand, skin side out.

steps.title: The sixth priest carries the innards and the lower legs
steps.stepSummary: The sixth כהן carries the קרבים in a vessel, with the כרעים placed on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sixth priest carries the innards, which are placed in a vessel, with the lower legs on top of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the parts of the animal with the sixth כהן, who carries the innards and the lower legs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Innards cannot simply be held in the hand, so they are carried in a בזך (vessel). The כרעים rest on top. With this, every part of the lamb has been assigned to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Innards, the intestines
A vessel or bowl
The lower legs

phrases.english: The sixth – with the innards, which are placed in a vessel,
and the lower legs on top of them, from above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of the animal's parts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sixth כהן carries the innards in a vessel, with the lower legs on top.

steps.title: The seventh, eighth, and ninth priests carry the flour, the griddle-cakes, and the wine
steps.stepSummary: Three more כהנים carry the items that accompany the תמיד: the סולת, the חביתין, and the יין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The seventh carries the fine flour. The eighth carries the griddle-cakes. The ninth carries the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the animal's parts are all assigned, the משנה lists the three כהנים who carry the other offerings that go with the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סולת is the מנחה that comes with the תמיד, and the יין is for its נסכים. The חביתין is the daily מנחה of the כהן גדול, offered half in the morning and half in the evening.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine flour for the מנחה that accompanies the תמיד
The כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering
Wine for the נסכים (libations)

phrases.english: The seventh – with the fine flour.
The eighth – with the griddle-cakes.
The ninth – with the wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the animal's parts to the offerings that go with it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seventh, eighth, and ninth כהנים carry the סולת, the חביתין, and the יין.

steps.title: The priests place everything on the ramp, salt it, and go to recite שמע
steps.stepSummary: The nine כהנים put their items on the lower western half of the כבש, salt them, and go to לשכת הגזית to say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went and put the items on the lower half of the ramp, on its western side, and salted them. Then they went down and came to the Chamber of Hewn Stone to recite שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends this stage of the עבודה. The pieces are set down and salted, and the כהנים pause to go say קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pieces are not yet burned on the מזבח. They wait on the lower half of the כבש, on its west side. Salting is required for קרבנות, and the כהנים then leave for תפילה before the עבודה continues.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
They salted them
The Chamber of Hewn Stone in the מקדש
The recitation of the שמע

steps.whatToRemember: Nine כהנים carry the תמיד: six carry the animal's parts and three carry the flour, the חביתין, and the wine. Everything is placed on the lower western half of the ramp and salted, and then the כהנים go to say שמע.

phrases.english: They went and placed them
from halfway up the ramp and below, on its western side.
And they salted them,
and they went down and came
to the Chamber of Hewn Stone to recite Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the carrying procedure begun in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All items are placed on the lower western half of the כבש and salted, and the כהנים go to לשכת הגזית for קריאת שמע.

steps.title: How the lamb was tied: a foreleg with a hind leg, like עקידת יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא explaining that the lamb was tied with a foreleg bound to a hind leg, like עקידת יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: a foreleg and a hind leg are tied together, like עקידת יצחק בן אברהם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It quotes a ברייתא that explains how the lamb was tied before שחיטה, which the משנה mentioned earlier in this פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said the lamb was tied (מעקדין) without saying exactly how. The ברייתא explains that one front leg was tied to one back leg. The model for this is עקידת יצחק, which is where the word עקידה comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Binding, tying a front leg to a back leg
The binding of Isaac by Abraham

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the tying of the תמיד was modeled on עקידת יצחק. That is why the משנה uses the word מעקדין.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A Tanna taught:
A foreleg and a hind leg,
like the binding of Isaac, son of Abraham.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא and returns to the tying procedure from the start of the perek.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lamb was tied with a foreleg bound to a hind leg, like עקידת יצחק.

steps.title: Why didn't they tie up the lamb?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the lamb was not tied with all four legs together, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: they did not tie up the lamb. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a short line from the משנה and asks why this rule exists. This sets up the next step, where two אמוראים give answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only told us what they did not do. It did not explain why. The גמרא wants the reason behind this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Tying up an animal with all four legs bound together
A young lamb (here, the קרבן תמיד)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: They would not tie up the lamb.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה. Instead of tying all four legs together, they bound one front leg to one back leg (Step 9).

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of how the lamb was bound, now asking why full tying (כפיתה) was avoided.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the כהנים did not tie the lamb with all four legs together.

steps.title: Two reasons: disgrace or copying the nations
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree. One says tying disgraces holy things. The other says it copies how idol worshippers bring offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree. One said: it is because of disgrace to holy things. The other said: it is because the person would be walking in the ways of the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question with two different reasons for not tying the lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is about respect: trussing up a holy animal like a bundle disgraces it. The second reason is about not copying idol worship, since that is how the nations tied their offerings. The תורה says not to walk in their ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Disgrace or disrespect to holy things
The customs and practices of the nations (idol worshippers)

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda disagree:
One said: because it is a disgrace to holy things.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם דִּמְהַלֵּךְ בְּחוּקֵּי הָעַמִּים.
phrases.english: And the other said: because he would be walking in the ways of the nations.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 with a disagreement between two אמוראים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either disgrace to holy things, or copying the practices of the nations.

steps.title: The practical difference: silk or a golden thread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons. The answer: tying the lamb with silk or with a gold thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them? There is a difference when he tied it with silk. Or, alternatively, with a thread of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to a different result in practice. It then gives a case where they do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying with silk or gold is not disgraceful, so the 'disgrace' reason would allow it. But it is still the way of the nations, so the 'ways of the nations' reason would forbid it. The answer gives two examples of this same idea: silk, or else a gold thread.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?
Silk
A thread (cord) of gold
Alternatively, or also

steps.confusionAlert: Silk and gold are not two separate disagreements. They are two examples of the same point: a fancy tie that is not disgraceful but still copies the nations.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
There is a difference between them
where he tied it with silk.
Alternatively, with a thread of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds a practical case where the two reasons of Step 11 lead to different results.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tying with silk or a gold thread is not disgraceful but still copies the nations, so the two opinions would disagree about it.
steps.whatToRemember: Not tying the lamb has two possible reasons: respect for holy things (בזיון קדשים) or not copying the nations (חוקי העמים). They differ about a fancy tie made of silk or gold.

steps.title: Thirteen tables, eight of marble in the slaughter area
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere: there were thirteen tables in the מקדש. Eight marble ones stood in the slaughter area, where the innards were washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: there were thirteen tables in the מקדש. Eight were of marble, in the slaughter area, and on them they washed the innards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic from our משנה, the washing of the innards on marble tables. It brings a משנה from elsewhere that lists all the tables in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה mentioned marble tables for washing the קרבים. This outside משנה gives the bigger picture: there were thirteen tables, and it starts with the eight marble tables in the slaughter area.

keyTerms.meaning: Tables
Marble
The slaughter area in the עזרה, north of the מזבח
They rinse or wash
Innards (intestines) of the animal

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in a different מסכת, שקלים.

phrases.english: There were thirteen tables in the מקדש.
Eight were of marble, in the slaughter area,
on which they would wash the innards.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שׁוּלְחָנוֹת הָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to our משנה's marble tables for washing the innards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were thirteen tables in the מקדש. Eight marble tables in the slaughter area were used for washing the innards.

steps.title: Two tables west of the ramp: marble and silver
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: two more tables stood on the west side of the כבש. The marble one held the limbs, and the silver one held the כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two were on the west side of the ramp, one of marble and one of silver. On the marble one they placed the limbs, and on the silver one the service vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה keeps listing the tables. Now it describes two tables near the ramp of the מזבח and what each one was used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These tables connect to Step 8, where the כהנים set the parts of the תמיד down near the ramp. The marble table held the limbs before they went up on the מזבח. The silver table held the כלי שרת used in that day's service.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Silver
The limbs of the קרבן
Service vessels used in the מקדש

phrases.english: Two were on the west side of the ramp,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ וְאֶחָד שֶׁל כֶּסֶף.
phrases.english: one of marble and one of silver.

phrases.aramaic: עַל שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ נוֹתְנִין אֶת הָאֵבָרִים,
phrases.english: On the marble one they would place the limbs,
and on the silver one, the service vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of tables from the משנה quoted in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: West of the כבש there was a marble table for the limbs and a silver table for the כלי שרת.

steps.title: Two tables in the entrance hall for the showbread
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues: in the אולם there were two tables, one of silver and one of gold. The לחם הפנים was placed on the silver one before it went in and on the gold one after it came out.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the Entrance Hall, on the inside, by the opening to the Sanctuary, there were two tables, one of silver and one of gold. On the silver one they put the showbread on its way in, and on the gold one when it came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the outside משנה about the thirteen tables. Now it describes two tables that stood in the אולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each table had a different job. Fresh לחם הפנים rested on the silver table before it was brought inside. The old bread, coming out after a week on the holy שולחן, was put on the gold table. The next step gives the reason for this order.

keyTerms.meaning: The Entrance Hall in front of the Sanctuary
The showbread, twelve loaves kept on the golden שולחן all week
Its entering, the bread's trip into the Sanctuary
Its leaving, the bread's trip out of the Sanctuary

phrases.english: And in the Entrance Hall, two on the inside
by the opening of the Sanctuary

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֶׁל כֶּסֶף וְאֶחָד שֶׁל זָהָב.
phrases.english: one of silver and one of gold.
On the silver one they place
the showbread on its way in,
and on the gold one on its way out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָאוּלָם שְׁנַיִם מִבִּפְנִים עַל פֶּתַח הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of tables from the quoted משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Silver table for the לחם הפנים going in, gold table for it coming out

steps.title: We go up in holiness, never down, plus the golden table inside
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that the outgoing bread goes on gold because מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין. It ends with the thirteenth table, the golden שולחן inside, where the לחם הפנים always rests.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we raise things up in holiness and do not bring them down. And one table of gold was inside, on which the showbread always rested.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason for the silver-then-gold order, then names the last table on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the bread has rested on the golden שולחן inside, putting it back on silver would lower its status. So when it comes out, it goes on gold. The golden שולחן inside completes the count of thirteen tables.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise holy things up in status and never lower them
Always, constantly

steps.whatToRemember: The rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין explains why the bread goes from silver, to the golden שולחן, to gold. Its status never drops.

phrases.english: For we raise up in holiness and do not bring down.
And one of gold inside,
phrases.notes: This is the golden שולחן inside the היכל, the thirteenth table.

phrases.english: on which the showbread is always.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the arrangement in step 15 and finishes the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holy items may be raised in status but not lowered

steps.title: Why marble tables in a wealthy place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the use of marble: the מקדש should never look poor, so why not make every table of silver or gold?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is no poverty in a place of wealth, why did they make marble ones? Let them make them of silver, let them make them of gold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's description of marble tables. It points to the principle that the מקדש should always be run in a rich way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The principle אין עניות במקום עשירות says the מקדש should never use cheaper materials. Marble is cheaper than silver or gold. So the marble tables seem to break this principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all (opens a strong logical point)
There is no poverty in a place of wealth; the מקדש should never look poor
Marble

phrases.english: Since there is no poverty in a place of wealth,
why did they make ones of marble?
Let them make ones of silver,
let them make ones of gold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the marble tables mentioned in the quoted משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that some tables were made of marble
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The principle אין עניות במקום עשירות requires rich materials, so marble should not have been used

steps.title: Metal heats up
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of names, רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק answers that marble was used because metal heats up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא said in the name of רבי אסי, and רבי אסי in the name of רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק: because it heats up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Marble was chosen for a practical reason, not to save money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silver or gold would get hot and could harm the meat placed on it. So using marble does not break אין עניות במקום עשירות. It was the right material for the job.

keyTerms.meaning: Heats up, makes hot

steps.whatToRemember: The rule against looking poor gives way when a cheaper material does the job better.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥinnana said in the name of Rabbi Asi,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אַסִּי בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Asi in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak:
Because it heats up.
phrases.notes: "It" is the metal. Silver or gold gets hot, and marble does not.

steps.title: Where the morning lamb was slaughtered, and the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to our משנה, which says the morning תמיד was slaughtered at the northwest corner, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The morning one was slaughtered at the northwest corner. From where are these words derived?

steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives an exact spot for slaughtering the morning תמיד. The phrase מנא הני מילי asks for the source of that detail. This sets up רב חסדא's answer.

steps.title: 'Two by day' means facing the day
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns from the פסוק 'שנים ליום' that the תמיד is slaughtered facing the daylight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Because the verse says 'two by day', meaning opposite the day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the source. He reads the words 'שנים ליום' as telling us where the lamb should stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply, 'ליום' just means 'each day'. רב חסדא also reads it as 'facing the day', so the lamb is slaughtered toward the daylight. That is why the morning lamb has its own set spot.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also teaches that 'שנים ליום' means the תמיד is slaughtered facing the daylight.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: 'Two by day' means facing the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב חסדא just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא read 'שנים ליום' as 'facing the daylight.' Now an older source, a ברייתא, reads the פסוק the same way. This gives his explanation outside support.

steps.title: Maybe the words just mean two lambs each day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: maybe 'שנים ליום' only means the daily duty of two lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means facing the day? Or maybe it only means the duty of the day, two lambs every day?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reading. Maybe 'שנים ליום' simply tells us to bring two lambs each day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'two by day' sounds like a count: two lambs per day. If so, the words teach nothing about which way to face. The ברייתא has to show why its special reading is needed.

steps.title: The daily count is already written elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: Another פסוק already says one lamb in the morning and one in the afternoon, so 'שנים ליום' must teach facing the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the תורה says 'One lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the other lamb you shall offer in the afternoon,' the daily duty is already stated. So how do I use 'two by day'? To mean facing the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The daily duty is already written in another פסוק, so these words must be teaching something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next פסוק already tells us to bring one lamb in the morning and one in the afternoon. The תורה does not repeat itself for no reason. So 'שנים ליום' is free to teach a new rule: slaughter facing the daylight.

steps.whatToRemember: Because the daily count of two lambs is written in a separate פסוק, 'שנים ליום' teaches that the תמיד is slaughtered facing the daylight.

steps.title: How facing the day works, morning and afternoon
steps.stepSummary: The morning תמיד is slaughtered at the northwest corner and the afternoon תמיד at the northeast corner, each at the second ring.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? The morning תמיד was slaughtered at the northwest corner, at the second ring. The afternoon one was slaughtered at the northeast corner, at the second ring.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows how 'facing the day' works in practice. The morning and afternoon lambs are slaughtered in different spots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sun moves during the day, so the place of slaughter changes too. In the morning the lamb is at the west side, and in the afternoon at the east side. This also explains our משנה, which said the morning תמיד was slaughtered at the northwest corner.
